newsitem.title: USA: Chinese-American Locke installed as Wash. governor.
newsitem.headline: Chinese-American Locke installed as Wash. governor.

text.p: Veteran Democratic politician Gary Locke, the son of immigrants, was inaugurated as Washington's 21st governor Tuesday, the first Chinese-American in any state to hold that title.

Locke, 46, formerly the top elected official in the state's most populous county, was surrounded by family members as he took the oath of office and succeeded one-term Democrat Mike Lowry after easily winning last November's election.

His election as the first Asian-American governor outside Hawaii sparked intense media interest around the Pacific Rim and a diplomatic dust-up when representatives from both China and Taiwan were invited to the inaugural ceremony.

Locke's protocol director Brent Heinemann resolved the dispute by arranging for China's representative to sit with the international consular corps on the statehouse floor while the Taiwanese delegation sat near Locke's family in the balcony.

Taiwanese officials are not given official diplomatic recognition in the United States, but Heinemann said the state was not bound by such distinctions. China and Taiwan are both important trading partners for Washington state.
Locke, one of five children born to Chinese immigrants in a Seattle housing project, has said that a near-fatal shooting of his father, a grocer, was among the factors that drove him into politics.
Locke did not learn to speak English until kindergarten but went on to graduate from Yale University and Boston University law school.
He was a deputy prosecutor and then served 11 years in the state legislature before being elected executive of King County, which includes Seattle.
